headline: Sri Lanka’s AML/CFT framework under international scrutiny as APG evaluation begins
body: Sri Lanka’s efforts to strengthen its financial system, combat money laundering and counter terrorist financing have entered a crucial phase with the commencement of the third Mutual Evaluation Conference of the Asia/Pacific Group (APG) on Money Laundering in Colombo. The inaugural event, held on Monday (26) under the patronage of Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya and Deputy Minister of Digital Economy Eranga Weeraratne, marked the beginning of an international assessment of the country’s Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing (AML/CFT) framework. The evaluation is significant for Sri Lanka as its ability to prevent financial crimes, enforce laws and maintain transparent financial transactions has implications for international confidence, investment flows and the integrity of its financial system. Addressing the event, Prime Minister Amarasuriya stressed that the assessment would demonstrate the progress Sri Lanka has made in combating financial crimes and meeting international standards. She warned that the erosion of public trust in financial institutions and corruption posed serious threats to a country’s economic and political stability. Transparency, accountability, effective institutional coordination and strong law enforcement were essential to safeguarding the financial system and restoring public confidence, she said. The Prime Minister reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to strengthening the country’s AML/CFT framework and addressing emerging financial risks. Initial discussions during the conference focused on money laundering and terrorist financing risks, legal reforms and national strategies, involving the AML/CFT National Committee, its Task Force and relevant government institutions. The Attorney General’s Department, Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption, Sri Lanka Police, Customs and the Central Bank’s Financial Intelligence Unit also discussed ways to improve risk management and institutional coordination. Emerging threats, including fraud centres, human trafficking, offshore financial risks linked to the Colombo Port and Special Economic Zones, and the potential misuse of non-financial businesses, professions and non-profit organisations, received attention. The APG assessment visit, scheduled from October 25 to November 6, 2026, will examine Sri Lanka’s AML/CFT framework, National Risk Assessment and institutional performance.
